newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Khaleda calls strike in southeastern Bangladesh.
newsitem.headline: Khaleda calls strike in southeastern Bangladesh.

text.p: Bangladesh's main opposition leader Begum Khaleda Zia on Saturday called for a daylong strike in southeastern districts on Tuesday to protest against what she said was "government-led terrorism."

"I ask you all to make the dawn to dusk strike in greater Chittagong division a complete success in common protest against government-led terrorism and failure of the ruling (Awami League) party on all fronts," Khaleda told tens of thousands of followers in Chittagong port city.
"May 6 will serve as a warning to this autocratic government and will be followed up, if necessary, with tougher actions," she said.
At least 100 police and other security men stood guard as the leader of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) and former prime minister spoke, amid cheers and loud applause, witnesses said.
Khaleda criticised the government of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina as being a "planted agent of a foreign power," meaning India, and said the BNP would resist any "hegemonist" move against Bangladesh.

"We will protect our independence and sovereignty at all costs," Khaleda said, adding that the ruling party was conspiring to let India use Bangladesh's territory and ports for transporting goods and military equipment.
"This government has failed on all fronts, starting from foreign policy to law and order," Khaleda said.
"It was driving a steam roller against political opponents, killing and arresting our followers," she alleged.
The BNP chief reiterated that her party would not take part in any future election unless current Chief Election Commissioner, Abu Hena, was removed.
"He helped to rig past elections and will do so in future polls. This is why they (Awami league) are giving him a clean bill," Khaleda said.
BNP lost to Hasina's Awami League in June 1996 general elections, which were billed free and impartial by local and international monitors.

She blamed the current problems in the insurgency-infested Chittagong Hill Tracts on the "government's kneel-down policy towards India," and warned aganist any move to pull out troops from the region.
"Nor shall we allow the government to remove (Bengali-speaking) settlers from the Hill Tracts," Khaleda added.
Removal of settlers has has been demanded by the tribal Shanti Bahini guerrillas

"If the government does not heed warnings, we will be compelled to call for a much tougher campaign to unseat them," said Abdullah al-Noman, former minister and senior leader of the BNP in Chittagong.
